claims.statement: THE DERIVED WORD, AND IT BREAKS NOTHING. The `rework` status word itself is 12/08's (`src/store/workflow.ts` — set when a bound gate's LAST decision is a rejection with no later submission, excluded from READY_STATUSES and from CLOSED_TASK_STATUSES); this task's own decision was GAPS ONLY, so it is credited, never rebuilt. What 12/06 proves is the bounded promise: the word is HONEST (not done, not blocked, not accepted) and the existing derivations still read correctly beside it — views.test.ts pins the leg status, the leg gate and the goal exhaustion against a rework-owed node, and `ann check` stays clean at the captured sha, so one human rejection never becomes a journey-wide failure.

`next` AND THE LOOK-BACK SAY REWORK — never a plain continue-leg. `AdvanceView.action` gains `rework-needed` and `advance()` derives it BEFORE the closure fallthrough, so the old `closure-needed` (whose remedy is transfer/defer, and which the driver DRAFTS A CLOSURE for) can no longer be produced for a rejected gate. Its detail names the task, the gate, and the human's feedback VERBATIM, and disclaims both wrong moves by name ('neither fresh work to dispatch nor a leg to close'). `LookBack.rework` mirrors DEFERRED end to end — one derived read (`Commands.reworkWork()`) carried to `ann next`, `ann journey` and `/api/journey`, shown BESIDE the state lines and never replacing them. Ready work still WINS: a sibling keeps the derivation at continue-leg while the owed rework stays visible in its own section.

THE DRIVER'S RULES REFLECT IT — RECORDED AS A NAMED LANDING, not a refusal. An explicit `run!` naming a rework-owed task is landed by `execRun`'s pre-flight at its BOUND gate with `wrote: []` and the human's feedback quoted; a bare `run!` is refused by the pre-existing derivation guard; and the boundary arm drafts NOTHING (`boundary-rework`) — the driver writes no closure and authors no task. The pre-flight reads the DERIVED word over both gates: the old check read `gateState(id,'grill')` only, so a task whose CONFIRM gate was the rejected one passed straight through and was driven as fresh work — that hole is closed and pinned by its own test. `rework` is deliberately NOT added to `validateProposal`'s closed-status list: it is open work (CLOSED_TASK_STATUSES excludes it), and calling it closed would be a semantic lie that halts the loop.

THE UI SHOWS THE REJECTION AND THE HUMAN'S OWN WORDS. The page gains its own REWORK OWED section (CSS + markup + `renderRework()`), each row naming the task, the leg, the REJECTED gate and the feedback verbatim, and DRILLING into that node with the gate in hand. The card's `next:` line appends the feedback (`reworkWhy`) instead of a bare status; the CLI card (`nodeCardLines`) prints REWORK OWED + `feedback:`; `ann next`/`ann journey` print the section. Verified on the real CLI against a rejected-gate fixture (`ann confirm` shows the gate, the rejection date and the feedback) and against the served page, whose bytes were fetched over HTTP to confirm the section ships.

DERIVED ONLY — no new event type, no new state, no new write path. Nothing was added to vocab, no writer was added, and the reject bound (3/gate) and the F-AC16/closure semantics are untouched: the two surviving `closure-needed` branches still fire for genuinely unmet legs, pinned by unchanged tests. DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED PLAN, recorded deliberately: the plan's section 4 included a `Store.readiness()` rework blocker, and it was DROPPED after implementation showed `Store.readiness()` is the FRAME'S EXECUTION SEAM, not display-only — the blocker would have stopped `frame.ts` and disabled the LOCKED, TESTED rework rung (a `rejected` tail re-obtains the gate, pinned by frame.test.ts). `Store.readiness()`, `frame.ts` and `frame.test.ts` are therefore untouched. The residual is honest and visible: a rework row still prints `executability READY`, which is the ENGINE's answer (the frame can run it) and not the human's; AC-4's requirement — that the rejection and its feedback be shown — is met by the REWORK section and the card. Tests prove the word, the next/look-back line, the driver landing, and the no-regression cases; the full suite is green and check/verify are clean at the captured sha; a mutation of the derivation wording kills exactly one test.
